item.title: Spooky Spiders! — Sat Oct 10, 2:00 PM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Does October make you think of all things creepy and crawly? If so, join Ranger Marissa in looking for some creepy, crawly spiders! We will learn about what types of spiders can be found at Elk Knob, where they can be found, and different ways you can catch them. If you make 7 observations on the iNaturalist app on any smart device, you will have the opportunity to earn an NC Spider Search patch! This program is open to all ages. All materials will be provided. Meet at the Park Office to begin.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Trail and Fireline Volunteer Workday — Sat Oct 10, 3:00 PM — William B. Umstead State Park - Crabtree Creek Entrance and Visitor Center
item.description:
Join us for a fireline and trail maintenance workday to help protect the outdoor spaces we love! Come get a hands-on experience learning about prescribed fire in State Parks while giving back.
No experience is required and all materials will be provided. Please wear close-toed shoes and proper attire. Bring plenty of water and snacks.
If interested please register at: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/g/pgxzhbCa3X
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Fall Into Franklinville: History Talks at Riverside Park — Sat Oct 10, 4:00 PM — Riverside Park
item.description:
A community event celebrating history, place, and local heritage, featuring two history talks: "Deep River: A Hundred Years Hence, Its Voice Will Be Heard" by Ross A. Holt, and "The First 250 Years of Franklinville" by Mac Whatley. Part of a larger event, 4 p.m.-8:30 p.m., featuring complimentary apple cider and pastries, live weaving and spinning demonstrations, a community scarecrow competition, a town time capsule ceremony and a sunset screening of the movie Pocahontas.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Bath Towne After Dark — Sat Oct 10, 6:00 PM — Historic Bath
item.description:
Seasonal vignettes from Shakespeare to Edgar Allen Poe. Campfire ghost stories. Marquee Tent with the dramatic telling of local legends. Local youth theater group: Not Quite Shakespeare
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Nocturnal Wildlife Kids Hike — Sat Oct 10, 6:00 PM — Hanging Rock State Park
item.description:
Bring the kids out for a spooky nature story followed by a 1.0-mile hike around Hanging Rock Lake as we discover what shrieks, hoots and prowls in the dark. This program is suitable for all ages but is designed for kindergarten- 5th. To register for this program email andra-claire.greene@ncparks.gov.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Sunset Big Canoe Paddle — Sat Oct 10, 6:00 PM — Falls Lake State Recreation Area - Beaverdam Access
item.description:
Join the crew and paddle a Big Canoe, seating up to 14-passengers. We'll have the life vests, paddles and a short orientation before paddling as the sun sets at the Beaverdam Recreation Area of Falls Lake. Please follow signs to the boat ramp. Please bring plenty of water and dress for outdoors.

item.title: Night Hike - History of Land Conservation — Sat Oct 10, 6:30 PM — Chimney Rock State Park - Rumbling Bald Access
item.description:
Join a park ranger for a guided hike along the Rumbling Bald Trail and discover how conservation, recreation, and community partnerships have shaped this special landscape.
During the hike, we’ll explore the role of ecotourism and how responsible outdoor recreation can connect visitors to the natural world while supporting the long-term protection of our public lands. Learn about the history of land conservation efforts that helped shape the area and contributed to the formation of the state park, as well as the ongoing work to conserve and steward these important natural resources.
Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a headlamp or flashlight.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: The Battle of Shallow Ford: An Exhibition of Watercolors and Words — Sun Oct 11 — Welborn Gallery
item.description:
On Display September 3 – Octobe 30, 2026
This collection of “watercolors” by master craftsman Rick Jones is accompanied by storyboards of “words” by artist and writer, Marilyn Ingram. The story, unfolding during a time where there were no cameras, cell phones, or even a typewriter, is told through the eyes of artists, field correspondents who would paint, draw or write a journal. The paintings include scenes at the Shallow Ford and nearby battle area, Moravian settlements along the great wagon road, and annual commemoration in Huntsville, NC. The words are researched through works including “Records of the Moravians” and NC State Archives. This exhibition is presented in partnership with The Lewisville Area Arts Council and was supported by the America 250 NC Community Grant.
An opening reception will be held September 3 from 5-7pm at the Yadkin Cultural Arts Center.
Refreshments will be served.
Free Admission, all are welcome to attend.

We have designed an escape room with a series of puzzles and riddles that lead you through the history of the region and NC State Parks. You will have 1 hour to solve the clues to create a timeline of the area's history and secure the key to escape. Registration is required. To sign up for a day and time please call 252-357-1191. Gather your friends or family (max. 10 people) if you are up for the challenge.

This ranger-led excursion will help you identify wading birds, shorebirds, raptors, and seasonal migrants while exploring some of the area's premier birding locations. Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.
We develop and distribute skills to navigate the Information War on truth and democracy.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Oct 13 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Tue Oct 13, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Oct 13, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:

Join us for games, crafts and coloring, sensory tables, and toddler-friendly activities including a leaf hunt, acorn crafts, and special animal meet and greet! This is a walk-up activity and is rain or shine at the park Visitor's Center. RSVP is encouraged to be up to date on changes to the program.

item.title: Fall Program: Elizabethan Brewing — Tue Oct 13, 2:00 PM — Roanoke Island Festival Park
item.description:
Humanity’s oldest friend, Elizabethans, had a love for drinks and played a significant part in their daily lives! From entertainment to daily survival, Englishmen of the past had to brew a lot of drinks to keep up! Come by the EII to see what historical beer and ale were made of and how it was made!

item.description:

Our students, volunteers, and staff consistently say that their most memorable memories at DCF are the conversations they shared over a wheelbarrow of mulch or while tackling weeds in a bed of carrots together. Absolutely no farming experience is necessary, and no Duke affiliation is required. We have tasks for most ages and abilities.

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Wed Oct 14, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Oct 15 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

Join us at the Transylvania Heritage Museum in Brevard for our new exhibit celebrating America's 250th anniversary. Discover how Revoluntionary War veterans, including Transylvania County Patriots, carried the spirit of liberty from battlefields into the rugged Appalachian frontier. Through artifacts, stories and hands-on experiences - including our Revolution Era Garden - explore the journey from conflict to community in the mountains we call home!
Open Thursday through Saturday 12 p.m. to 4 p.m. Free and open to all. Donations accepted
Source: NC Cultural Resources
